key_insight: CoReMem treats memory for coding agents as an investment: its expected future usefulness must justify the effort of writing and reading it. It also considers when using available memory can save work during a task.
problem_solved: Coding agents working on successive tasks must preserve useful knowledge about an evolving repository before they know the next task, without accumulating memory that costs more to maintain and consult than it saves.
method: Introduce Coding-Repository Memory (CoReMem), a framework for managing memory across successive coding tasks.
Use prospective valuation to balance anticipated future usefulness against memory-writing and memory-reading costs.
Guide memory design and actor adaptation, including decisions about when to act on available memory as a task unfolds.
impact: For practitioners, CoReMem offers a way to reason about memory efficiency rather than simply storing more context. The supplied abstract is truncated, so quantitative performance gains cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: Timeline of successive coding tasks on an evolving repository, with memory passed between tasks.
Balance scale contrasting expected future benefit with writing and reading costs.
Decision flow showing when an agent should consult and use memory.
Memory-card icons highlighting selective retention rather than indiscriminate storage.
paper_title: CoReMem: Cost-Internalizing Memory for Successive Coding Tasks with Prospective Valuation
paper_authors: Peiwen Li, Harshit Verma, Sophia Zhou, Haiwen Wang, Ngoc Bui
